title: "Week 4 – The menu and the declaration"
case: housing
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 3](../../slides/housing-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The second week of the housing-audit case works the menu of defensible analyses, one decision at a time, and ends on the one analysis that you would defend, declared in the preregistration block of your report before it runs. Read the specification menu before the class meets. In class you explore the menu and send one exploration to the class chart, read the chart against the curve of the claim, and then declare, run and report. The rest of the week reads the curve and the replication with new data at a slower pace, and finishes the first case report.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Specification menu](../../cases/housing/menu.qmd) | Before class. The estimand statement, the eleven decisions at three levels, the five on which the curve keeps more than one option and the 64 specifications that they make, the worked example, and the rules for declaring and reporting a result. | 30 minutes |
| Slides, the menu and the methods in Part 3 | In class. The ground rules of the menu: change one decision at a time, and read the reason when an option is refused. Then a difference in proportions and the linear probability model set against the logit, with the optional run on odds ratios, standard errors for a 0/1 outcome and the randomisation test if the class wants it. | 20 minutes |
| Task 4 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-4-menu) Task 4, then [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results) | In class. Call `try_spec()` with no arguments for the reference specification, then three or four times more, changing one argument at a time, and compare the tries with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for an option off the curve, such as `model = "three_group"`, to read why it is refused. Send the try that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`; it appears on the class chart as an open circle. | 25 minutes |
| Slides, [Part 4](../../slides/housing-one-day.html#/part-4-multiverse-replication-and-preregistration) | In class. The class chart against the curve of 64 with the published result and the five analysts on it, what moved the estimate, the SCORE replication with new names and the power of the two designs, the critics of the multiverse, and what a preregistration settles and what it leaves open. | 40 minutes |
| The preregistration block in your report, or [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-5-preregistration) Task 5 | In class. Complete the block before you run anything: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, one option for each decision, a sentence from your causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Render the report and keep the rendered copy, then fit the specification with `run_spec()` and send it with `report_result()`; it appears on the chart as a filled circle. | 25 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) | Reading the curve, the reference marks, what moved the estimate, and the displays beside the curve: the other outcomes and the Black names, the subgroups, and the randomisation distribution. | 40 minutes |
| [Audit experiments](../../companion/experiments.qmd#sec-ri), sections 5 and 6, and [the replication](../../cases/housing/index.qmd#sec-replication) | Randomisation inference, power, and why significant estimates from small studies tend to be too large; then the design and the result of the preregistered audit of 3,050 housing authorities that SCORE ran, and how to read it beside the curve. | 50 minutes |
| [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd), sections 1 to 8 | Where multiverse analysis came from, the three purposes that a multiverse can serve, the debate of 2025–26 read against this small curve on which every specification agrees while the replication failed, robustness against replicability, and the multiverse in teaching. | 60 minutes |
| Your report | Render the report of the workspace with all five tasks complete, the preregistration block as it stood before the run and the result beneath it. This is the first case report of the term. | 30 minutes |

**By the end of the session** you have an exploratory and a declared mark on the class chart of the housing-audit case, the place of your declared result among the 64 specifications of the curve, a preregistration that was completed before its specification ran, and the first case report rendered.
